title: The First 90 Days: What Actually Changes When a Fractional CFO Joins the Business
linkedin:
Most owners expect a fractional CFO to walk in and have an opinion by Friday.

That is not how the first ninety days actually go, and the businesses that get the most value understand this before they start.

The pattern we see across owner-led businesses is a steadier build than the fantasy version.

Weeks one to three are diagnostic, not advisory. No recommendations yet, just a proper look back through the last twelve months of trading to see where margin is genuinely made and where it quietly leaks. Most owners are working from instinct that was accurate two or three years ago and has not been re-tested since.

Weeks four to eight shift to visibility. A rolling cash flow forecast gets built. Reporting gets tightened into something that actually reflects trading reality. None of this replaces what a good bookkeeper or BAS agent already does well, it sits on top of that work.

By around day ninety, the value stops being about any single deliverable and starts being about rhythm. Decisions on pricing, hiring or a new piece of equipment get tested against a forecast before they are made, not explained after the fact.

The businesses that get the most out of a fractional CFO partnership treat the first quarter as a build phase, not a rescue.

A question we hear often from Brisbane and Queensland business owners: what actually happens once a fractional CFO joins the business?

It is not an instant transformation. The first three weeks are spent on diagnosis, understanding twelve months of trading in detail before any recommendations are made. This protects the business from advice built on outdated instinct rather than current numbers.

Weeks four to eight shift to visibility, building a proper cash flow forecast and tightening reporting so the numbers an owner sees each month actually reflect trading reality. This work sits alongside the bookkeeper or BAS agent, not in place of them.

By around day ninety, a monthly rhythm is in place. Pricing, hiring and equipment decisions get tested against a forecast before they are made, not justified after the fact.

For owner-led businesses across the East Coast turning over one million to thirty million dollars a year, understanding this build before starting saves a lot of misplaced expectations in month one.
